title: Handoff orchestration
summary: Specialist agents transfer control to each other through handoff tool calls. There is no central orchestrator: the receiving agent owns the task. It is interactive by default and returns to the user when an agent does not hand off.
useIf: A conversation should move between specialists (triage, billing, returns) and the current specialist should own the user until it decides to hand off.
avoidIf: A primary agent should keep ownership and only borrow help (use agent-as-tool), or work is non-interactive and fixed (use sequential or a graph).

explain.md: Build with `HandoffBuilder(name=..., participants=[...]).with_start_agent(triage).add_handoff(a, [b, c])` in Python or `AgentWorkflowBuilder.CreateHandoffBuilderWith(triage).WithHandoffs(triage, [math, history])` in .NET. A handoff is triggered by a **special tool call**. By default every agent can hand off to every other; `add_handoff` narrows which agent may take over next, but the topology remains a mesh because agents share context. Handoff supports only `Agent` with **local tool execution** [[tr25]].

explain.md: **Interactive by default.** When an agent answers without handing off, Python emits a `request_info` event with a `HandoffAgentUserRequest`; the user's reply (or `HandoffAgentUserRequest.terminate()`) resumes the run. **Autonomous mode** is experimental: when an agent does not hand off, the workflow feeds it a continuation prompt (`User did not respond. Continue assisting autonomously.`) until it hands off, a termination condition fires or the per-agent turn limit is reached (.NET default **50** autonomous turns per agent; `WithAutonomousMode(turnLimit, continuationPrompt)`; `with_autonomous_mode()` in Python) [[tr25]].

**Context sync.** Agents do not share a session. Each participant broadcasts its responses and user inputs to all others. Tool-related content, including the handoff calls, is not broadcast: only user and agent messages are. In Python, text, inline data, URIs, hosted files and vector stores are kept for user messages while non-user messages keep text only. For approvals that arrive hours later, give the builder `checkpoint_storage` and resume with the checkpoint id then the responses [[tr25]].

blocks.code:
var workflow = AgentWorkflowBuilder.CreateHandoffBuilderWith(triage)
    .WithHandoffs(triage, [refund, orders, returns])   // triage can route to all
    .WithHandoffs([refund, orders, returns], triage)   // and they can return
    .WithAutonomousMode(turnLimit: 10,
        continuationPrompt: "Continue assisting the user.")   // experimental
    .WithTerminationCondition(conv => conv.Any(m => m.Text?.Contains("RESOLVED") == true))
    .Build();

from agent_framework.orchestrations import HandoffBuilder, HandoffAgentUserRequest

workflow = (
    HandoffBuilder(name='support', participants=[triage, orders, returns, refund],
                   checkpoint_storage=storage)
    .with_start_agent(triage)
    .add_handoff(triage, [orders, returns])
    .add_handoff(returns, [refund])                 # only returns may reach refund
    .add_handoff(orders, [triage]).add_handoff(refund, [triage])
    .build()
)
async for ev in workflow.run('My order 1234 arrived damaged', stream=True):
    if ev.type == 'request_info' and isinstance(ev.data, HandoffAgentUserRequest):
        reply = input('You: ')
        # resume: workflow.run(responses={ev.request_id:
        #     HandoffAgentUserRequest.create_response(reply)}, stream=True)

whereToUse: Customer support: triage hands to orders, returns or refund specialists
Tutoring or advisory chats with subject specialists
Back-office flows where the owner of a case changes as the case evolves
Hours-long approvals with checkpointing, since tool approvals surface as request events

use: The user talks to one specialist at a time and ownership should transfer
Specialists have different tools and instructions
A person is in the loop each turn (interactive default)
avoid: A primary agent must keep ownership: use agent-as-tool
Agents are remote or cannot run tools locally: handoff supports only `Agent` with local tool execution
Handoff loops are possible with no limit: bound autonomous mode and set termination
flips: You need no human between turns: autonomous mode, with a turn limit and a termination condition (experimental)
Routing must be centrally controlled and auditable: use a custom workflow or group chat with a manager

pitfalls.symptom: Agents ping-pong the user between each other
pitfalls.cause: Overlapping instructions and unconstrained handoff rules
pitfalls.fix: Narrow `add_handoff` edges, make specialist scopes disjoint, set a termination condition

pitfalls.symptom: A specialist is unaware of tool results from another
pitfalls.cause: Tool content and handoff calls are not broadcast; only user and agent messages are
pitfalls.fix: Have agents state tool findings in their replies

pitfalls.symptom: Handoff fails on a remote agent
pitfalls.cause: Handoff supports only `Agent` with local tool execution
pitfalls.fix: Wrap the remote agent as a tool, or restructure

scenarios.title: Support desk with specialists
scenarios.situation: A support desk has triage, order status, returns and refunds. A refund needs approval above a threshold. Chats are live. Refund requests only after a return is registered.
constraints: Ordering rule: refund only via returns
unknowns: Can the user talk to several specialists in one chat?
scenarios.question: How do you design it?

options.name: Handoff with triage as start, `add_handoff` rules so only returns reaches refund, approval-required refund tool, checkpoint storage
options.why: Ownership moves with the case, the graph enforces who may take over, and approvals arrive as request events that survive restarts.
options.tradeoff: Mesh context broadcasting grows tokens, and routing quality depends on specialist prompts.

options.name: Triage agent with the other three as tools
options.why: Triage stays accountable and the design is simple.
options.tradeoff: Specialists never talk to the user directly; triage relays everything.

options.name: Group chat with a manager
options.why: Adds rounds and a manager call for a conversation where one agent should own each turn.
options.tradeoff: Better for review loops than for live support.

flips.if: Routing is a simple lookup by customer tier
flips.then: Use a conditional edge in a custom workflow.
Consider autonomous mode with a turn limit, still gated by approval-required tools.

scenarios.takeaway: Handoff fits when the conversation owner should change.

scenarios.title: Autonomous overnight triage
scenarios.situation: Tickets arrive overnight with no human. An agent should classify, enrich and resolve simple ones, handing complex ones to a specialist that works the case.
unknowns: How many turns does a typical resolution take?
Is the risk of an autonomous error acceptable?
scenarios.question: Do you use autonomous handoff?

options.name: Yes, with a low `turnLimit`, a termination condition, per-ticket budget alerts and approval-required write tools
options.why: It fits the shape (no user) and the limits bound loops and cost.
options.tradeoff: Experimental feature: expect API changes, and failures need alerting.

options.name: A custom workflow with explicit routing and one agent per stage
options.tradeoff: More design work and less flexibility for odd tickets.

options.name: Autonomous mode with the default 50-turn limit and no termination
options.why: A stuck agent could spend up to 50 turns per ticket.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable only for experiments with a spend cap elsewhere.

flips.then: Keep a human gate and use the interactive default.

flips.if: Policy forbids experimental features in production

scenarios.takeaway: Autonomous means unattended: bound turns, terminate on a state and alert on spend.

quiz.q: Which statement best distinguishes handoff from agent-as-tool?
options: Handoff keeps the primary agent in charge
In handoff the receiving agent owns the task and no central orchestrator exists; with agent-as-tool control returns to the primary agent
They are the same pattern with different names
quiz.explain: The docs distinguish control flow, task ownership and context management: handoff transfers ownership, agent-as-tool keeps it with the primary.

quiz.q: Which are true for handoff? Select all.
options: It supports only `Agent` with local tool execution
Handoff tool calls are broadcast to every participant
quiz.explain: Tool content, including handoff calls, is not broadcast; only user and agent messages are synchronised.

flashcards.back: A special tool call by the current agent. The receiving agent then owns the task.
